title: Issue stock options
summary: Grant stock options to team members including board approval, option agreements, and Carta recording.

parts.title: Verify 409A is current
parts.guidance: Compare the proposed US option grant with the valuation’s date, stock class and conditions. Check financing discussions, transactions and material developments since that date against the report’s assumptions. If they undermine the basis for the proposed exercise price, resolve the need for a refresh with the valuation adviser and counsel before proceeding with the grant.

parts.title: Draft board consent for grant
parts.guidance: Draft the grant consent from the proposed recipient, share count, option type, exercise price, vesting and intended grant date. Check plan capacity and the valuation supporting the price. Use the applicable corporate approval route, resolving uncertainty with counsel, and highlight deviations from standard terms so the decision-makers can assess the actual grant proposal.

parts.title: Board approves and signs the grant consent
parts.guidance: The authorized board or delegate reviews the final grant schedule and signs the required consent through the applicable corporate process. Check recipient, quantity, price, dates and special terms against the proposal. Establish when approval is effective, and bring later changes back through the required decision path before they enter the agreement or equity records.

parts.title: Generate option agreement
parts.guidance: Populate the option agreement from the effective authorization and governing plan. Match the recipient, security, quantity, price, vesting, exercise terms and dates, including approved deviations. Resolve conflicts between the agreement, plan and consent with counsel. The final package should give the recipient the agreed grant terms and the governing plan they reference.

parts.title: Send for employee signature
parts.guidance: The equity administrator sends the final agreement and governing plan to the intended recipient for signature. Give the recipient a contact for questions and route requested changes back through the grant’s legal and corporate decision process. Track execution against the agreement’s requirements and link the completed signature record to the grant, distinguishing a sent invitation from acceptance.

parts.title: Record grant on Carta
parts.guidance: Enter the completed grant in the equity system from its effective authorization and executed documents. Match recipient, quantity, exercise price, grant date, vesting and plan allocation, then reconcile remaining capacity. The authorized equity administrator links the consent, agreement and valuation reference to the entry and resolves discrepancies between the system and the legal records.

metadata.supportReason: Carta API can record grants. Board consent and option agreements need human review. System drafts materials and tracks.

geoNotes.summary: ESOPs need a shareholders' special resolution under Companies Act s.62(1)(b) and are taxed as a perquisite at exercise on a registered valuation — DPIIT-recognised startups can defer that perquisite tax by up to five years.
UK startups grant EMI options — an HMRC-approved scheme with capital-gains treatment; the company agrees a valuation with HMRC in advance (the rough 409A analog) and notifies grants to HMRC.

Real options were historically tax-hostile, so most startups grant VSOPs (virtual options, cash-settled); § 19a EStG — expanded by the 2024 Zukunftsfinanzierungsgesetz — now defers the dry-income tax on genuine employee shares for qualifying startups.

French startups grant BSPCE — founder-company warrants reserved for young companies, with capital-gains-style taxation and no social charges for the employer; the Bpifrance (state investment bank) encyclopedia page is the canonical guide.

Options are granted under a company plan with shareholder approval; for IAPMEI-recognised startups the Lei 21/2023 regime defers taxation of qualifying plans to liquidity with a partial exclusion — the lever that makes Portuguese ESOPs workable.

Grants are board-approved under the plan; for CCPCs the employee's taxable benefit is deferred until the shares are sold and the 110(1)(d) deduction can halve it — CRA's security-options guidance is the canonical reference.
